BEST_BET.rationale: Its step change comes from geometry, not from heroic cell physics, so it is the one that survived every red-team correction: 0.37 vs 3.95 pJ/b delivered (~11x; 5.5x with random placement, 15x at 1 mm), because the bit skips the PHY, interposer and TSV stack. The system claim fell from ~190 to ~92 W/GPU at the 16-tier x 1 b planning case (48-169 W range), but it pays at 1 b/cell and needs neither MLC nor >=32-tier yield. Oxide 2T0C is the most mature oxide cell in the set (reported >200 s at 95 C, >1e12 cycles), and oxides have no hole conduction (no GIDL), so a deeper negative hold is a real knob. Re-running models/hot-side-memory.py: the 1e-4 tail cell plans at 12.5 aA at 125 C against a 22.5 aA ceiling for 1 b (unmitigated 45.6 aA fails, so the series write gate or the -0.7 V hold must work). Refresh is 1.4-3.6 s at 105-125 C, ~225x rarer than Si: refresh-light, not refresh-free. The FATAL backside-overlay objection is designed around with carrier-last. What remains is foundry-side (overlay, killer defects, In/Ga/Zn contamination, a BSPDN partner; Intel 18A is the only U.S. line), and it is not a cost step ($4.6-12/GB). For a two-founder team that is the best ratio of physics odds to prize.
BEST_BET.experiment: Gate A+ by M11: 2T0C coupons in IGZO / In-poor IGZO / IGO / Ga-free ZTO, single vs series write gate, -0.5 vs -0.7 V hold. Each is measured after the post-bond heat/H sequence AND a real D2O-labelled 350-400 C fusion bond. On >=1e5 cells per split: drift at 1/10/100 s at 85/105/125 C, write-T1/read-T2 maps (dT +/-30 K), RTN at 1 us-1 s, the directly measured 1e-4 retention quantile, and SIMS H/D. Then the M18 demo: 2 IGZO tiers on finished CMOS (sky130 in the portfolio; 22FDX standalone), RO shift <=1%, Vt <=10 mV, 1,000 h at 105 C, and measured array+sense energy extrapolated to the port.
BEST_BET.cost: ~$240k for Gate A+ standalone ($1.00M full plan). In this portfolio ~$150k rides on the shared oxide-tail lot plus $85k for the oxide-on-CMOS carrier.
BEST_BET.kill: M11: kill the capacity claim if every split, including the real-bond, series-gate and -0.7 V-hold splits, fails any one of three tests: 1e-4-tail retention <1 s at 105 C (tail >22.5 aA at 125 C), drift sigma >75 mV at 1 s/105 C, or 1e-4 RTN quantile >100 mV. M18: kill BEOL tiers (carrier-only) if RO shift >1% or Vt shift >10 mV cannot be recovered. Cut the energy claim below 4x if measured bitline+sense energy extrapolates to >0.9 pJ/b at the port.

FASTEST_PROOF.rationale: It is the only decisive experiment in the portfolio with no fabrication and no new physics. It runs on 4 DRAM Bender stations plus 2 open Antmicro DDR5 RDIMM testers, costs ~$124k and gives a binary at M6. A GO sets two things. First, a publishable data asset: ~9x refresh-energy cut on DDR5 RDIMMs at 85 C with chipkill kept (model: 285 ms central / 194 ms pessimistic safe interval vs the 32 ms spec, 6.0-8.9x; 6.1-20x range), ~13x on retired DDR4 behind CXL, 0.98 -> 0.11 W per 64 GB. Second, a measured VRT-coincidence and multi-bit-event census. That census decides whether the raw-BER-1e-4 ECC budget holds on real silicon: the 1.88x margin (Cs 5.4 -> 2.7 fF) that MARGIN STACK, PIXEL-STACK, HOT-SIDE (RS(36,32)+BCH t=23) and AND-STACK MLC all assume. The flag leg is killed and module value is small (~$3.9/module over 5 yr), so this is the proof and the instrument, not the company. The same Bender rigs deliver MARGIN STACK's error-pair study.
FASTEST_PROOF.experiment: Phase 1, M0-6, has two legs. Retired-DDR4 raw retention maps: 150 modules screened over >=30 lots per vendor, 60 deep-mapped at 0.128-4 s x 45/65/85 C x 4 patterns. DDR5 leg: >=24 1a/1b RDIMMs read through JEDEC ECS counts and post-SEC event maps inverted to raw BER. Also: VRT per-codeword coincidence over 1,000 h on 20 modules, a dwell-time (RTN) spectrum from 20 s-20 min re-maps, a failure-mode census of every multi-bit event, a 1 h grade vs 1,000 h hold servo test, and hammer at relaxed refresh with RFM.
FASTEST_PROOF.cost: ~$124k, decisive at M6 (Phase 2-3 CXL soaks bring the standalone plan to $946k; not funded in this portfolio until the raise)
FASTEST_PROOF.kill: NO-GO if the RS-8 (chipkill) safe interval including VRT is <4x the part's JEDEC window at 65 C, or multi-chip events are >10% (or a new mechanism grows >2x at relaxed refresh), or the 1 h grade holds on <95% of modules over 1,000 h. On NO-GO every cell model reverts from the 3.72-sigma ECC budget toward 7-sigma design. Revival: re-run on oxide cells, whose retention tail sits 1e3-1e4x to the right.

MOONSHOT.rationale: It has the highest ceiling left after the red team: 64 tiers x 2 b = 2.62 Gb/mm2, 5.9x 1-beta (8.8x at 96 x 2 b in two decks). Bits/$ is ~2.3x vs 2026 1-beta (2.2-2.6x), refresh power ~25x lower at 1 s, and no EUV, because density comes from tier count instead of lithography. The cell physics closes numerically: the write-FET tail is <=5 aA at a -3.0 V hold even at 160 mV/dec, against a 17 aA budget. The single-film closure was killed as topologically impossible. The two-film notched write pocket needs three modules with no precedent: selective IPD ALE in a notch, recess-fill-etch-back of an oxide semiconductor, and IGZO-safe slit replacement. P(closure) ~20%. That is a process-integration problem with many knobs, which is exactly where persistence works. Honest discount: against a projected 2032 incumbent bits/$ is only 1.1-1.4x (1.2-1.6x at 96 tiers), NEO's NAND-process DRAM is ~3 years ahead, and Macronix's 3D AND estate sits around it.
MOONSHOT.experiment: GO #1A (M9, planar, on the shared oxide-tail lot): per-tier CR >=0.57 at sigma <=0.045 over >=50 cells; write-FET hold tail <=17 aA on >=1e4 devices at 85 C; 4 levels holding >=1 s with <=78 mV tail drift; cross-temperature 2-b BER <=1e-4 at dT +/-10 K; <=30 mV after 1e9 neighbour writes. GO #1B (M14-16): a 2-tier vertical closure coupon (250 nm e-beam holes, SiO2/poly-SiGe/SiO2/SiN stack, notched write pocket) with write-then-read and no ring-to-read-channel short, ring hold <=100 aA at 85 C at -3.0 V, per-tier CR >=0.57, and FIB/TEM of the notch.
MOONSHOT.cost: In this portfolio, $30k of planar add-on structures plus a $100k closure coupon, funded only if M9 tails pass. Standalone, ~$0.4M of direct spend reaches GO #1B and the full plan is $970k.
MOONSHOT.kill: M9: if the write-FET hold tail is >100 aA at 85 C on 1e4 devices even with the series option, or CR <0.57 or sigma >0.045, drop 2 b and the single-etch leg. M18: if the 2-tier coupon has not closed (short-free write-then-read, hold <=100 aA, CR >=0.57), kill single-etch and fall back to the coaxial per-tier cell (~1.5-2.5x bits/$).

honest_framing: The study found 12,857 ideas but one durable opening: in DRAM, reading a bit is a solved circuit problem and holding it is a materials-statistics problem. The new room is where oxide semiconductors (no hole conduction, zeptoamp medians) let you trade capacitor charge for local gain and stacked tiers. All 181 red-team objections were answered and nothing died on physics, but nearly every headline roughly halved. Against a projected 2032 incumbent no concept still claims more than ~1.6x bits per dollar. The surviving step changes are energy (~11x vs HBM delivered), refresh (~9-13x on commodity DRAM) and density at high tier counts (5.9x and 4.6x 1-beta), not cheap bits. Persistence can beat integration and process problems (notch modules, bond warp, hydrogen budgets, layout, yield), because those have many knobs and iterate. It cannot change image-force barrier lowering, oxide trap emission kinetics or the shape of an RTN tail; it can only search for a different material, which is slower and odds-limited. So the honest plan is to measure the oxide tails first, then build the cell those tails allow, with HOT-SIDE MEMORY as the bet that pays even at 1 bit per cell.
biggest_unknown: The tail statistics of scaled amorphous-oxide (IGZO-class) transistors after the full <=400 C hydrogen/thermal and bonding budget. It has three parts: (a) RTN step-amplitude quantiles at 1e-4 to 1e-9 in 0.01-0.02 um2 devices, from ns (CDS) to s (retention) timescales; (b) storage-node leakage at the aA level at the 1e-4 / 2e-5 quantile at 85-125 C; (c) whether those tails are independent between neighbouring devices, which decides whether series write gates square them. Published data are medians (~zA extrapolated Ioff, ~200 s median retention at 95 C), but every pass line sits in the tail: HOT-SIDE <=22.5 aA at 125 C, AND-STACK <=17 aA, MARGIN STACK <=586 aA aged and RTN <=44 mV, PIXEL-STACK RTN <=20/40 mV at 15 ns, DIODE-TOWER <=25 mV, CHARGE-RIVER <=30 e-. One measurement campaign sets the size of the step for 7 of the 10 concepts.
